findings.name: Content-Security-Policy
findings.reason: CSP is present but should be reviewed: 'unsafe-inline' allowed for scripts without a nonce or hash.
findings.purpose: Restricts which sources the browser may load scripts, styles and frames from, limiting the impact of injected content.
findings.risk: Without it, an XSS flaw (if one exists) is easier to exploit. Absence alone does not prove XSS exists.
findings.mitigation: Define a policy starting from default-src 'self'; use nonces or hashes instead of 'unsafe-inline'; consider Report-Only first.
findings.verification: Re-run the tool and check the header; test pages in the browser console for CSP violations.
findings.limitation: The tool does not fully parse CSP semantics or evaluate every directive.

findings.name: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.reason: Final URL uses HTTP; browsers ignore HSTS over HTTP, so it cannot be evaluated here. Re-test the HTTPS URL.
findings.purpose: Tells browsers to use HTTPS only for the site, reducing downgrade and SSL-stripping exposure.
findings.risk: Without it, a user's first or later plain-HTTP request may be intercepted by a network attacker.
findings.mitigation: Serve it on HTTPS responses with max-age of at least 15552000; add includeSubDomains only after checking subdomains.
findings.verification: Re-run against the HTTPS URL and confirm max-age; browser dev tools show it under response headers.
findings.limitation: Only meaningful over HTTPS; preload status is not checked.

findings.name: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.purpose: Stops browsers from guessing (MIME-sniffing) content types, preventing some content-confusion attacks.
findings.risk: Uploaded or reflected content may be interpreted as an executable type in some scenarios.
findings.mitigation: Send 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' and ensure correct Content-Type on all responses.
findings.verification: Re-run the tool; confirm the value is exactly nosniff.
findings.limitation: Only the checked URL is evaluated; other routes may differ.

findings.name: X-Frame-Options
findings.purpose: Controls whether the page can be embedded in frames, mitigating clickjacking.
findings.risk: A page that can be framed may be used in a clickjacking attempt against logged-in users.
findings.mitigation: Use CSP 'frame-ancestors' (preferred); optionally also send X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN.
findings.verification: Re-run the tool; optionally try framing the page from a local test HTML file you control.
findings.limitation: Whether framing is actually harmful depends on page functionality.

findings.name: Referrer-Policy
findings.reason: Effective policy 'unsafe-url' may leak full URLs to other origins.
findings.purpose: Controls how much referrer (URL) information is sent to other sites.
findings.risk: Full URLs, which may hold tokens or identifiers in paths or queries, could leak to third parties.
findings.mitigation: Use 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or stricter; avoid putting secrets in URLs.
findings.verification: Re-run the tool; check outgoing Referer headers in browser dev tools.
findings.limitation: Policies set via <meta> tags or per-element attributes are not seen.

findings.name: Permissions-Policy
findings.purpose: Restricts access to powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation) for the page and embedded frames.
findings.risk: Embedded third-party content may request features the site does not need.
findings.mitigation: Disable unused features, e.g. 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()'.
findings.verification: Re-run the tool and review the directive list.
findings.limitation: Directive contents are not validated; support varies across browsers.

disclaimer: Findings are observations and potential risks based on one HTTP GET response. A missing or weak header does not by itself confirm a vulnerability, and this report is not a security score or a complete assessment.
